Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National Retaining the incumbent regional chairman is the surest bet for Ashanti NDC Source : GNA 17 November 2026 5:15am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Mohammed Yakubu, the Member of Parliament (MP) for Ahafo Ano South-East, has described the re-election of Mr Andrews Nana Akwasi as Ashanti Regional Chairman of the NDC as the surest bet for maximising the party’s votes in the Election 2028.
He explained that keeping the current regional leadership in place would help consolidate the gains already made and provide the party with a stable base from which to pursue its electoral ambitions in the Ashanti region.
Speaking to the Ghana News Agency, after the regional executive elections, the MP said it was time for the past executives and the currently elected ones to deduce more winning strategies ahead of the 2028 general elections.
He said the period offered an opportunity for both past and newly elected executives to reflect on the lessons of the previous contest and work out more effective and winning strategies that would strengthen the party’s fortunes.
Mr Yakubu noted that a divided house could not progress and that the leadership must prioritise reconciliation to have a formidable force to ensure victory in the general elections.
He therefore urged the party’s leadership to reach out to those who lost the elections and bring them on board so that the NDC could present a united front in the region.
To him, the chairman-elect deserved the victory, acknowledging the good work he did in the 2024 general elections in ensuring that the NDC votes appreciated in the region and moved the Parliamentary seat to seven in the region.
He said the outcome reflected the confidence that the party faithful had in the regional leadership and the efforts made to strengthen the NDC’s presence in the Ashanti Region.
The MP enumerated some development projects in his constituency, citing the building of a 24-Hour Economy Model Market, construction of over twenty boreholes in various communities, and building new school blocks, among others.
Mr Yakubu called on the Ahafo Ano South-East constituents to exercise restraint while he delivered on the mandate for which he was voted for.
